metaDescription: Five 40V cordless lawn edgers compared, blade edgers and trimmer edger combos, on blade size, depth control, battery included and edge quality.
expertTake: The Greenworks 40V 8 inch brushless edger is our top pick because a steel blade, a curb wheel, tool-free depth control and a four-year warranty on the tool and battery suit crisp edges along concrete. The Wild Badger 13 inch trimmer edger is the value pick for people who want one tool for trimming and edging. If your edges are overgrown and deep, skip a battery edger and rent a gas stick edger for the first cut.
introParagraphs: A cordless lawn edger cuts a clean vertical line between grass and a driveway, walk or bed, the finishing touch that makes a lawn look maintained. Two very different tools claim the name: a dedicated blade edger and a trimmer that flips on its side. They produce different edges.

This guide explains how each design cuts, why depth control and a guide wheel matter, and what battery platform means for ownership. The quick picks sit above, and the detailed reviews below show which tool suits which edge.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 8 in Brushless Lawn Edger Kit, 4.0Ah
products.description:
The Greenworks is a true blade edger: an 8 inch steel blade spins vertically and slices a trench along the edge, while a curb wheel rides the concrete to keep the line straight. That is the part that makes it more precise than a string trimmer turned sideways, which tends to wander. A brushless motor adds torque and longer life.

Tool-free depth adjustment lets you set the cut depth without hunting for a wrench, and it handles uneven or sloped ground. It includes a 4.0Ah battery and charger, unlike the bare-tool version of the same edger, which excludes both. The warranty is four years on tool and battery, the longest in this guide.

Check blade wear each season, clear soil from the housing and store the battery indoors. It suits owners with long concrete edges.
products.bestFor: Owners with long concrete or paver edges who want a precise blade cut with a complete kit.
pros: 8 inch steel blade cuts a clean vertical edge
Curb wheel rides concrete to keep the line straight
Tool-free depth adjustment sets cut depth quickly
Four year warranty covers tool and battery
cons: A single-purpose tool that does not trim
Blade wears faster in sandy or gritty soil
Storage space needed for a separate machine

products.name: HART 40V 8.5 in Cordless Walk-Behind Edger, 4.0Ah
products.description:
The HART is a walk-behind edger with an 8.5 inch blade, slightly larger than the Greenworks 8 inch blade, and a brushless motor. It lists a 20 inch cutting swath, a wheel-spacing figure that describes its working footprint. A larger blade can cut a little deeper in one pass, which helps on edges that have crept over.

The listing is brief compared with the Greenworks, with no stated depth system or warranty, so verify those before buying. It includes a 4.0Ah battery, the same capacity as the Greenworks kit.

It uses the HART 40V battery platform, so check that the packs will serve other tools you own. Clear the housing, check the blade and store the battery indoors. It suits owners in the HART ecosystem.
products.bestFor: Owners in the HART 40V ecosystem who want a slightly larger blade for deeper edges.
pros: 8.5 inch blade is larger than the Greenworks 8 inch
Brushless motor gives more torque and longer life
20 inch swath describes a stable walk-behind stance
4.0Ah battery included in the kit
cons: Listing gives no depth system or warranty details
HART battery platform is less common than Greenworks
Single-purpose edger with no trimming function

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX 13 in String Trimmer Edger, Telescoping Pole
products.description:
This BLACK+DECKER is a trimmer that converts to an edger in seconds, with a telescoping pole, a PowerCommand dial that trades power for runtime and an automatic feed spool. The PowerDrive transmission is designed to send more motor power to the string, and the head spins up to 8500 rpm.

A string edge is fast and forgiving but not as crisp as a blade, because the string flails rather than slices. It is a good fit for light, regular edging on a lawn that is kept up. Against the Greenworks 13 inch trimmer, it adds a power dial and telescoping reach.

The included battery has a state-of-charge indicator and charges in two hours or less. The warranty is three years. Replace line as it wears, clean grass from the guard and store the battery inside.
products.bestFor: Light, regular edging on a maintained lawn where one tool needs to trim and edge.
pros: Converts from trimmer to edger in seconds
PowerCommand dial switches between power and runtime
Automatic feed spool needs no bump feeding
Three year limited warranty and fast charger
cons: String edge is less crisp than a blade edge
Struggles on overgrown or deep edges

products.name: Greenworks 40V 13 in Cordless String Trimmer and Edger Kit
products.description:
The Greenworks combo tool has a seven-position pivoting head, which is its main advantage over a basic trimmer: you can set the head at the angle that suits trimming under a deck or edging along a walk. A telescoping shaft from 40 to 52 inches fits different heights, and it uses 0.065 inch auto-feed line.

It weighs a stated 7.8 pounds, a little more than the Wild Badger's 6.6. A steel edging guide helps keep a line. Like all string tools it cuts a softer edge than the dedicated blade edger.

A 3-year tool and 2-year battery warranty is solid, and the 40V battery fits other Greenworks tools. Replace line, clean the head and store the battery indoors. It suits users who want more head angles.
products.bestFor: Owners who want flexible head angles and a telescoping shaft for trimming and edging.
pros: Seven head positions suit under-deck and edging work
Telescoping shaft fits users of different heights
Steel edging guide helps keep a straight line
Shares a 40V battery with other Greenworks tools
cons: String edge is less crisp than a blade edger
7.8 pounds is heavier than the Wild Badger
2.0Ah battery limits runtime on long edges

products.name: Wild Badger Power 40V 13 in Cordless String Trimmer and Edger
products.description:
The Wild Badger is the lightest here at 6.6 pounds, a real advantage when you edge a long border. It spins at 6500 rpm, below the BLACK+DECKER's 8500, which means a gentler cut. The listing claims about 30 minutes of runtime and includes two packs of trimmer line.

It is a plain 2-in-1 with auto feed and a 13 inch path. A smaller maker means thinner support than the Greenworks or BLACK+DECKER, and the listing offers little detail on the head or warranty.

Line wears quickly at edging, so the spare packs are practical. Clean the guard and charge indoors. It suits cost-conscious owners.
products.bestFor: Cost-conscious owners who want the lightest 2-in-1 for short edging jobs.
pros: 6.6 pounds is the lightest tool here
About 30 minutes of runtime on one charge
Two packs of trimmer line are included
Auto feed spool avoids bump feeding
cons: 6500 rpm cuts less aggressively than the 8500 rpm BLACK+DECKER
Less established brand with unclear warranty
String edge is less crisp than a blade

buyingCriteria.explanation: A blade edger slices a vertical trench with a steel blade guided by a wheel, giving a crisp edge. A string trimmer turned sideways flails line, which is quicker but softer and less straight. For long concrete borders, a blade is better. The Greenworks 8 inch and HART 8.5 inch are blade edgers, while the others are trimmers.

A larger blade cuts deeper in one pass, and depth control matters because lawns grow over borders. Tool-free depth adjustment makes changing settings easy. The HART uses an 8.5 inch blade and the Greenworks 8 inch with tool-free depth adjustment.
A curb wheel keeps a blade edger parallel to the pavement. Without it, the line wanders. The Greenworks edger has a curb wheel, and the string tools use an edging guide.

A 40V platform shares batteries across mowers and blowers. Amp-hours set runtime, and edging a long border drains small packs. The Greenworks and HART kits include 4.0Ah packs, while the trimmers use 2.0Ah.
A trimmer edger is lighter and reaches under shrubs. The Wild Badger weighs 6.6 pounds and the Greenworks combo 7.8. A blade edger is heavier but rolls on wheels, so you carry less.
Warranty reveals confidence in the battery. The Greenworks edger has four years on tool and battery, the BLACK+DECKER three, and the Greenworks combo three on the tool and two on the battery.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the vertical steel blade. A larger blade can cut deeper per pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: Capacity depends on motor torque, so 8 versus 8.5 inches is a small difference.

specDecoder.meaning: The speed of the blade or head with no resistance. Speed drops under load.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Greenworks edger lists 6500 rpm no load. Under load, speed falls.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without carbon brushes, giving more torque and longer life.
specDecoder.watchFor: Both blade edgers are brushless. The trimmers do not state it.

specDecoder.meaning: A wheel that runs against the pavement edge, guiding the blade.
specDecoder.watchFor: A string trimmer has no true curb wheel.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp-hours, the battery capacity that sets runtime.
specDecoder.watchFor: 2.0Ah packs limit jobs. The kits here range from 2.0 to 4.0Ah.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cut quality
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated blade from string tools and favoured blade edgers for crisp lines. The Greenworks 8 inch and HART led.

howWeEvaluated.title: Depth and guidance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at depth adjustment and guide wheels. The Greenworks's tool-free depth and curb wheel ranked highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared included batteries. The 4.0Ah kits beat 2.0Ah trimmers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and versatility
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed tool weight and function. The Wild Badger at 6.6 pounds was lightest, and the trimmers added trimming.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated coverage. The Greenworks edger's four years stood out.

cards.label: Blade edger
cards.text: Slices a crisp trench guided by a wheel, but only does edging. Includes the Greenworks 8 inch and HART 8.5 inch.

cards.label: Trimmer edger
cards.text: One tool that trims and edges, lighter but softer cut. Includes the BLACK+DECKER, Greenworks 13 inch and Wild Badger.

howToChoose.note: Pick a blade edger for crisp borders and a trimmer edger if you want one tool.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A curb wheel, steel blade and depth control to keep a straight line.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 8 inch with its curb wheel is the best, and the HART is the alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You edge long borders often. The Greenworks 8 inch gives the best precision and warranty.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You edge short stretches. The Wild Badger or BLACK+DECKER is enough.

maintenance.why: Gritty soil dulls steel. A worn blade tears rather than slices.
Packed soil adds drag and rust. A quick brush keeps it clean.
Short line cuts less. Fresh line restores the edge.
Cold reduces capacity. Store at partial charge.
Loose wheels throw off the line. Tighten them.

faq.q: Is a blade edger better than a trimmer edger?
faq.a: For crisp lines along concrete, yes. A trimmer edger is lighter and does two jobs.
A depth of about an inch to two inches is common. Set it to the edge's condition.

faq.q: Can I use a 40V edger on a large property?
faq.a: Yes, with spare batteries. Long borders can drain a single 2.0Ah pack.

faq.q: What does a curb wheel do?
faq.a: It rides the pavement edge, keeping the blade straight.
Every two to four weeks during growth keeps edges neat.

faq.q: Do I need a different battery for each tool?
faq.a: Within a platform, no. Greenworks 40V batteries share across tools.
